newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge rules Hinckley may not leave hospital.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge rules Hinckley may not leave hospital.

text.p: A federal judge rejected on Thursday a request by presidential assailant John Hinckley to leave St. Elizabeths Hospital for 12-hour, unsupervised visits each month with his parents.
"The court concludes that John Hinckley continues to present a danger to himself or others, and his motion must, therefore, be denied," U.S. District Judge June Green said in the 15-page decision.

Hinckley, 42, has been confined to the hospital for 15 years since he was found not guilty by reason of insanity in the March 30, 1981 shooting of President Ronald Reagan. He also wounded three others in the attack.
The judge held four days of hearings last week in which Hinckley's lawyer presented testimony from four psychiatrists or psychologists and from Hinckley's father in support of the request.

U.S. prosecutors called their own psychiatric expert, who said Hinckley may appear healthy but actually remains dangerous, and a woman pharmacist at the hospital who testified that Hinckley stared at her and would not leave her alone.
Green found that Hinckley still suffers from various mental illnesses and continues to deceive those treating him at the hospital.
She said he failed to disclose to the hospital staff the relationship he sought with the pharmacist and that he was considering a possible interview on a Barbara Walters television show.

"The severity of (Hinckley's) criminal conduct, and his conduct at the hospital since his admission in 1982 as well as his current behaviour, all militate against the conditional release he seeks," the judge said.
Since his commitment to the hospital, Hinckley at various times has sought some form of release, but the requests have all been denied or had to be withdrawn.
